> ## Judge Rotations
>
> Crew judge rotations adapt the existing judge scheduling model into a local-operator event surface.
>
> [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/judges.tsx]] selects a workout and renders the drag-and-drop judging grid plus publishing described in [[crew#Judge Rotations#Judge Assignments Grid]].
>
> [[apps/crew/src/server-fns/crew-judge-rotations-fns.ts]] keeps route imports lightweight while [[apps/crew/src/server/crew-judge-rotations.server.ts]] owns Crew event hydration, scoped rotation writes, and publishing through the versioned assignment helper.
>
> [[apps/crew/src/lib/crew/judge-rotations.ts]] keeps rotation expansion, validation, lane conflicts, and coverage summaries deterministic for the route and server.
>
> Publishing rotations creates a new active `judge_assignment_versions` row and materializes `judge_heat_assignments` under the advisory-lock flow from [[crew#Judge Assignment Version Publishing]].
>
> ### Judge Roster Eligibility and Imported Judges
>
> The judge roster includes every staffable volunteer on the competition team, whether account-backed or invitation-based, that is judge-eligible.
>
> `loadCrewJudgeVolunteers` builds the roster from the same membership + invitation union as [[crew#Roster Shifts Assignments]] ([[apps/crew/src/server/crew-roster-shift.server.ts#loadCrewRoster]]), so imported / manually-added volunteers (stored as `team_invitations` with no user account) appear alongside account-backed memberships. Organizers routinely import a batch of General volunteers intending to seat them as judges, so excluding General would leave the grid empty after a bulk import.
>
> Every judge is keyed by a canonical assignee id: the membership id (`tmem_`) for account-backed volunteers, or the invitation id (`tinv_`) for imported ones. `CrewJudgeVolunteer.membershipId` carries this canonical id so the grid keys judges unchanged. `competition_judge_rotations` and `judge_heat_assignments` each carry a nullable `membershipId` and a nullable `invitationId` (exactly one set), parallel to `volunteer_shift_assignments`. Saving, conflict validation, materialization, and active-assignment hydration all resolve through the canonical id, so invitation-based judges are assignable and publishable end to end. Day-of check-in / replacement remains membership-keyed and rejects accountless judges with a clear message until that flow is widened.
>
> ### Judge Assignments Grid
>
> The Crew judging UI ports wodsmith-start's two surfaces: a Gantt-style **Rotation Timeline** for pre-publish planning, and a heat-lane **Published Assignments** grid for post-publish fine-tuning.
>
> [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/judges.tsx]] renders a single page heading and then [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/judge-scheduling-container.tsx]], which owns the layout (workout selector, the gated Published Assignments section on top, the Rotations section below) and the local cell state. The Published Assignments section appears only once the workout has an active published version; the Rotations section is always shown for a workout with heats.
>
> The pre-publish surface is [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/rotation-timeline.tsx]] — a coverage grid of heats × lanes where organizers click a cell or "Add" to plan a judge's rotation across heats. Crew heat numbers are not guaranteed to start at 1 (the Heats setup UI has a global starting-heat control, see [[crew#Heats Page]]) and may have gaps, so the timeline keeps two spaces: the grid geometry runs in 1-based **display-index** space while stored rotations and the editor form fields (`startingHeat`) run in **actual heat-number** space. The timeline's `displayToHeatNumber` / `heatNumberToDisplay` maps convert at every boundary — cell clicks and rotation drops convert display→actual before reaching the editor, editor preview cells convert actual→display before matching grid keys, and column headers render actual heat numbers. The editor validates/clamps against the workout's real min/max heat numbers (`minHeat`/`maxHeat`), not a heat count — its zod schema is built per-instance so `startingHeat` is bounded to `[minHeat, maxHeat]`, `startingLane` to the max lane count, and `heatsCount` to the heat range, preventing saves that would expand to zero cells. Heats can also have differing lane counts: coverage is always computed from each heat's own `laneCount` (so the timeline's coverage % matches the RotationOverview), grid cells whose lane exceeds a heat's own lane count render as unavailable (assignments there would be dropped by `expandRotationToAssignments`), and the editor's live preview mirrors `expandRotationToAssignments` exactly — skipping heat-number gaps and cycling shift-right lanes per-heat — via a `heats` prop threaded from the timeline. [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/multi-rotation-editor.tsx]] is the per-judge rotation form (multiple collapsible rotation blocks with live preview), and [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/rotation-overview.tsx]] shows coverage metrics plus the [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/publish-rotations-button.tsx|Publish]] control. An "Event defaults" tray ([[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/event-defaults-editor.tsx]]) sets per-workout rotation defaults — default rotation length, stay-in-lane vs shift-right, and the minimum heat buffer — persisted via `updateCrewJudgeEventDefaultsFn` (scoped through Crew event manager access, not the team-membership permission path); its number fields autosave debounced (raw string state so clearing/retyping works, invalid values snap back on blur) with no success toast; typing an invalid value cancels any pending debounced save so a superseded value never fires, and prop-syncs are skipped while a field is focused so a refresh can't clobber mid-typing input. The timeline deliberately preserves its UI state (open editor, selection, expanded judges) across post-mutation loader refreshes — the container remounts it per workout via `key`, so only stale rotation-id selections are cleared when saves replace rotation rows. Coverage and expansion reuse [[apps/crew/src/lib/judge-rotation-utils.ts]] (`calculateCoverage`, `expandRotationToAssignments`, `filterRotationsByAvailability`), resolving each rotation to the same membership-or-invitation canonical assignee id, so multi-heat rotations with lane-shift patterns and buffer zones render exactly as in wodsmith-start.
>
> The post-publish surface keeps the per-cell heat-lane grid: [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/judge-heat-card.tsx]] and [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/draggable-judge.tsx]] provide the `@atlaskit/pragmatic-drag-and-drop` draggable judges and droppable lanes. Each grid cell (one judge in one heat + lane) is a single-heat rotation (`heatsCount = 1`, lane-shift `stay`); [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/judge-grid-utils.ts]] converts saved rotations to grid cells and back ([[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/judge-grid-utils.ts#rotationsToGridCells]], [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/judge-grid-utils.ts#gridCellsToRotationRows]]).
>
> Both surfaces persist rotations through the same canonical-id-aware path: every save (timeline editor, cell drop/move/remove, or rotation drag) replaces the affected judge's full rotation set via `saveCrewJudgeRotationsForVolunteerFn`, and the Publish button materializes them with `publishCrewJudgeRotationsFn`. Only the per-workout defaults tray adds a server function (`updateCrewJudgeEventDefaultsFn`).
>
> Draft `competition_judge_rotations` stay editable after publishing — saves are never blocked by an existing published version. A published version is an immutable snapshot keyed by its `versionId`; its `judge_heat_assignments` rows persist independently and carry `rotationId` only as provenance (a plain column, not a DB foreign key, and unused for active-assignment hydration). So adjusting the grid or timeline after publishing replaces the draft rotations, and re-publishing materializes the updated draft into a brand-new active version while prior versions stay intact for audit and rollback ([[crew#Judge Assignment Version Publishing]]).

/** A single rotation block to persist for a volunteer. */
export interface RotationDraft {

  minHeat: number

  maxHeat: number
  maxLanes: number
  /**

   * heat's own laneCount drives shift_right, so previews match the saved grid.

  heats: Array<{ heatNumber: number; laneCount: number }>
  availableJudges: CrewJudgeVolunteer[]
  /** All rotations grouped by canonical assignee id (membershipId) */
  rotationsByVolunteer: Map<string, CompetitionJudgeRotation[]>
  existingRotations?: CompetitionJudgeRotation[] // For editing - all rotations for this volunteer

  initialHeat?: number

  externalPosition?: { heat: number; lane: number; timestamp?: number } | null
  activeBlockIndex: number
  onActiveBlockChange: (index: number) => void
  eventLaneShiftPattern: LaneShiftPattern
  eventDefaultHeatsCount: number

  onSave: (membershipId: string, rotations: RotationDraft[]) => Promise<void>
  onSuccess: () => void
  onCancel: () => void
  onPreviewChange?: (cells: MultiPreviewCell[]) => void
  /** Called when judge selection changes (for highlighting existing rotations) */
  onJudgeSelect?: (membershipId: string | null) => void
}

/**
 * Form shape for multiple rotations. Judge selected once, multiple rotation
 * blocks managed with useFieldArray. This module-level schema is used only to
 * derive the form-values type — the resolver uses a per-instance schema built in
 * the component that also bounds fields to the workout's heat/lane range.
 */
const multiRotationSchema = z.object({
  membershipId: z.string().min(1, "Judge is required"),
  rotations: z
    .array(
      z.object({
        startingHeat: z
          .number()
          .int()
          .min(1, "Starting heat must be at least 1"),
        startingLane: z
          .number()
          .int()
          .min(1, "Starting lane must be at least 1"),
        heatsCount: z.number().int().min(1, "Must cover at least 1 heat"),
        notes: z.string().max(500, "Notes too long").optional(),
      }),
    )
    .min(1, "At least one rotation required"),
})

type MultiRotationFormValues = z.infer<typeof multiRotationSchema>

/**
 * Multi-rotation editor component with accordion-style UI.
 * Allows creating/editing multiple rotations for the same volunteer.
 * Each rotation block is collapsible with independent form fields.
 * Preview cells for ALL blocks with different visual treatment per block.
 */

  minHeat,
  maxHeat,
  maxLanes,
  heats,
  availableJudges,
  rotationsByVolunteer,
  existingRotations,
  initialHeat,
  initialLane,
  externalPosition,
  activeBlockIndex,
  onActiveBlockChange,
  eventLaneShiftPattern,
  eventDefaultHeatsCount,
  onSave,
  onSuccess,
  onCancel,
  onPreviewChange,
  onJudgeSelect,
}: MultiRotationEditorProps) {
  const isEditing = !!existingRotations && existingRotations.length > 0
  // When adding a new rotation (activeBlockIndex >= existingRotations length),
  // start with no blocks open - the new block will be opened when it's added
  // Otherwise, open the first block by default
  const isAddingNewRotation =
    isEditing && activeBlockIndex >= (existingRotations?.length ?? 0)
  const [openBlocks, setOpenBlocks] = useState<Set<number>>(
    isAddingNewRotation ? new Set() : new Set([0]),
  )

  const [isSaving, setIsSaving] = useState(false)

  // Schema bound to this workout's actual heat/lane range. Without these bounds a
  // user could enter a startingHeat outside [minHeat, maxHeat] or a startingLane
  // above maxLanes; the rotation would save but expand to zero grid cells.
  const boundedSchema = useMemo(
    () =>
      z.object({
        membershipId: z.string().min(1, "Judge is required"),
        rotations: z
          .array(
            z.object({
              startingHeat: z
                .number()
                .int()
                .min(minHeat, `Heat must be at least ${minHeat}`)
                .max(maxHeat, `Heat must be at most ${maxHeat}`),
              startingLane: z
                .number()
                .int()
                .min(1, "Starting lane must be at least 1")
                .max(maxLanes, `Lane must be at most ${maxLanes}`),
              heatsCount: z
                .number()
                .int()

content.content: 263:The pre-publish surface is [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/rotation-timeline.tsx]] — a coverage grid of heats × lanes where organizers click a cell or "Add" to plan a judge's rotation across heats. Crew heat numbers are not guaranteed to start at 1 (the Heats setup UI has a global starting-heat control, see [[crew#Heats Page]]) and may have gaps, so the timeline keeps two spaces: the grid geometry runs in 1-based **display-index** space while stored rotations and the editor form fields (`startingHeat`) run in **actual heat-number** space. The timeline's `displayToHeatNumber` / `heatNumberToDisplay` maps convert at every boundary — cell clicks and rotation drops convert display→actual before reaching the editor, editor preview cells convert actual→display before matching grid keys, and column headers render actual heat numbers. The editor validates/clamps against the workout's real min/max heat numbers (`minHeat`/`maxHeat`), not a heat count — its zod schema is built per-instance so `startingHeat` is bounded to `[minHeat, maxHeat]`, `startingLane` to the max lane count, and `heatsCount` to the heat range, preventing saves that would expand to zero cells. Heats can also have differing lane counts: coverage is always computed from each heat's own `laneCount` (so the timeline's coverage % matches the RotationOverview), grid cells whose lane exceeds a heat's own lane count render as unavailable (assignments there would be dropped by `expandRotationToAssignments`), and the editor's live preview mirrors `expandRotationToAssignments` exactly — skipping heat-number gaps and cycling shift-right lanes per-heat — via a `heats` prop threaded from the timeline. [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/multi-rotation-editor.tsx]] is the per-judge rotation form (multiple collapsible rotation blocks with live preview), and [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/rotation-overview.tsx]] shows coverage metrics plus the [[apps/crew/src/routes/events/$eventId/-components/judges/publish-rotations-button.tsx|Publish]] control. Fixed and verified. The crash was a pre-existing bug (from the earlier "Fix crew judge rotation previews" commit), not today's dropdown change — I confirmed by stashing my changes and reproducing it on the bare branch.

**Root cause:** `RotationTimeline` passed `heats={heatsWithAssignments.map(...)}` to `MultiRotationEditor` — a new array on every render. The editor derives its preview cells from that prop and reports them back via `onPreviewChange` → `setPreviewCells` in the timeline. So opening the editor closed a loop: timeline renders → new `heats` reference → editor recomputes previews → effect fires → timeline setState → render again, until React threw "Maximum update depth exceeded" (the Radix ScrollArea ref in the stack was just where React detected it).

**Fix:** memoized the array as `editorHeats` in `rotation-timeline.tsx` with a comment explaining the referential-stability constraint.

Verified in the browser: the judges page loads, "Add" opens the rotation editor with zero console errors, and the judge dropdown shows the new format — e.g. **"Brian Lee · 9 rotations"** with **"Last scheduled: Heat 9 · Event 2.00: Grace"** beneath.           control={form.control}
          name="membershipId"

            // Sort judges by rotation count (fewest first)
            const sortedJudges = [...availableJudges].sort((a, b) => {
